company.name: Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd
company.about: Emmvee Photovoltaic makes solar modules and TOPCon solar cells at plants in Karnataka, selling mainly to Indian independent power producers, commercial and industrial buyers and EPC contractors. It has about 10.3 GW of module and 2.94 GW of cell capacity and is adding a 6 GW integrated line due by March 2027. It is separate from other Emmvee Group businesses such as solar water heaters.

events.title: Stock falls 5.8% to ₹255 in a green-energy sell-off, about a third below its July high
events.details: Emmvee shares closed at ₹255.15 on 21 October 2026, down about 5.8%, and traded near ₹249 on 22 October as Indian renewable-energy stocks fell on a jump in crude oil prices and geopolitical tension. The stock was down about 17% from its 14 October close and about 33% below its 52-week high of ₹371.55, at roughly 12 times trailing earnings. No company-specific news explained the fall.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the de-rating came despite results that beat estimates, so sector sentiment and pricing worries are now driving the stock more than earnings.

events.title: China proposes export curbs on 12 solar technologies, including TOPCon know-how and wafer processes
events.details: China's commerce ministry published draft export controls on 12 solar manufacturing technologies. Polysilicon, thin-wafer (70 microns or less) and tandem-cell processes would be prohibited for export, and TOPCon, HJT and back-contact cell know-how and core equipment would need licences. Comments are open until 15 November 2026. Indian solar stocks fell on the news; one report linked Emmvee's 2% drop on 19 October to it.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the curbs could raise costs or delay Emmvee's planned 9 GW ingot-wafer plants and the commissioning of its new TOPCon cell line, which rely on Chinese equipment and know-how.

events.title: Shares fall 5% on results day despite a profit beat; down 7.7% for the week
events.details: Emmvee shares fell 5.04% to ₹284.45 on 15 October 2026, the day after its Q2 results, touching ₹275.95 intraday, about 8% down. Profit had come in above consensus, but gross margin eased from the previous quarter and module lines ran at only about 44% utilisation. The stock ended the week at about ₹277.10, down 7.73%, while the Sensex rose 1.91%.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the market focused on flat quarter-on-quarter profit and margin pressure rather than the year-on-year growth.

events.title: US trade commission rules Indian solar imports harm US makers; steep duties due 2 November
events.details: The US International Trade Commission made a final finding that imports of solar cells and modules from India, Indonesia and Laos have injured US producers. That allows the Commerce Department to issue anti-dumping and countervailing duty orders, expected on 2 November 2026, with preliminary rates for India reported at about 123% anti-dumping and 126% countervailing duty. Emmvee sells mainly in India and has little direct US exposure.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: Indian makers that relied on US exports may push more volume into the domestic market, adding to price competition for Emmvee.

events.title: Plans 9 GW ingot-wafer capacity for ₹5,000–5,500 Cr, phased over FY29 and FY30
events.details: With its Q2 results, Emmvee outlined plans to make its own ingots and wafers, the step before cells: 5 GW in FY29 and 4 GW in FY30, at an estimated cost of ₹5,000–5,500 crore. The company said it would fund the project mainly from internal accruals, though one report cited about ₹3,300 crore of debt, and that timing depends on clarity about government wafer-sourcing rules (ALMM List-III). Most hard-cost orders for the 6 GW cell and module expansion had been placed.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: full integration could protect margins if wafer rules tighten, but the spend is about a quarter of the market value and depends on access to Chinese technology.

events.title: Q2 FY27: revenue up 39% to ₹1,576 Cr, PAT up 61% to ₹382 Cr; order book 10.4 GW
events.details: For the September 2026 quarter, revenue rose 39.4% year on year to ₹1,576.4 crore, EBITDA was ₹556.9 crore, about a 35% margin, and profit after tax rose 60.6% to ₹382.0 crore, ahead of a consensus of about ₹360 crore. First-half profit was ₹762.3 crore, up 79%. The order book reached 10.4 GW after 1.5 GW of new orders. Finance costs fell to ₹9.5 crore from ₹55.2 crore. Net debt rose to 0.12 times equity from net cash in March as spending on expansion picked up.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: first-half EBITDA of ₹1,105 crore is about half the FY27 guidance, so the full-year target looks achievable.

events.title: First AGM as a listed company approves FY26 final dividend of ₹1 per share
events.details: Emmvee held its 19th annual general meeting, its first since listing, by video conference on 25 September 2026. Shareholders approved a final dividend of ₹1 per share for FY26; the ex-dividend date was 18 September. The FY26 annual report had been filed on 2 September. The payout is small relative to profit, consistent with the company keeping cash for its expansion programme.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: routine; the company is prioritising capacity spending over payouts.

events.title: Stock jumps more than 8% after Jefferies reiterates Buy and ₹440 target after meeting management
events.details: Emmvee shares rose more than 8% on 21 September 2026 after Jefferies reiterated its Buy rating and ₹440 target following meetings with management at its India forum on 17–18 September. Jefferies said it expects EBITDA to grow about 33% a year from FY26 to FY29 and noted that all six analysts covering the stock rated it Buy. The jump reversed part of a slide from the July high, but the stock did not regain that level.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: broker support has been a recurring driver of the stock's sharp moves since listing.

events.title: Jefferies raises target to ₹440 from ₹400, citing a discount to peers; stock up as much as 7%
events.details: Jefferies kept its Buy rating and raised its target price to ₹440 from ₹400, arguing that Emmvee trades at a large valuation discount to other listed Indian solar manufacturers. The shares rose 5–7% intraday. Earlier in August, HDFC Securities' retail research named Emmvee a pick of the week, suggesting buying at ₹315–330 with a base value of ₹360 and a bull case of ₹400.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: named broker targets of ₹360–440 sit well above the October price, so the gap reflects sector worries more than company numbers.

events.title: Stock jumps 10% to a record ₹371.55 after Q1 profit doubles; Jefferies lifts target to ₹400
events.details: The day after Q1 FY27 results, Emmvee shares rose about 10% to ₹371.55, still their 52-week high, about 71% above the ₹217 IPO price. Jefferies raised its target to ₹400, noting that EBITDA and profit beat its estimates by about 19% and 22%. The stock then drifted lower over the following three months, even as later results and broker upgrades came in ahead of expectations.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: this marked the peak of the post-listing rally; later results beats did not lift the price back to this level.

events.title: Q1 FY27: PAT doubles to ₹380 Cr on 51% revenue growth; record 35.2% EBITDA margin
events.details: For the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 51% year on year to ₹1,555.5 crore, EBITDA reached ₹548.1 crore at a record 35.2% margin and profit after tax rose 103% to ₹380.3 crore. Module output was about 970 MW and the order book about 9.9 GW. Management reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹2,200–2,400 crore and said earnings per watt were about ₹2.5 for modules and ₹6.5 for cells, with demand for domestically made cells expected to strengthen.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the cell line running near full capacity is what lifts margins, which is why the planned tripling of cell capacity matters.

events.title: ALMM List-II takes effect, requiring approved domestic solar cells in eligible projects
events.details: From 1 June 2026, India's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers for solar cells (List-II) came into force, meaning many government-backed and other covered projects must use cells from approved domestic makers. Along with domestic content rules for rooftop and farm-solar schemes, it supports demand and premium pricing for Indian-made cells. Emmvee is among the larger domestic TOPCon cell makers and is adding about 6 GW of cell capacity by March 2027.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: this is the main policy support for Emmvee's cell margins; any dilution of the rules would be a key risk.

events.title: FY26: revenue up 116% to ₹5,050 Cr, PAT up 193% to ₹1,082 Cr; stock hits 52-week high
events.details: In its first full-year results as a listed company, Emmvee reported FY26 revenue of ₹5,050 crore, up 116%, and profit after tax of ₹1,081.6 crore, up 193%, with an EBITDA margin of about 34%. March-quarter revenue rose 62% to ₹1,738.8 crore and profit rose 89% to ₹392.4 crore. The order book was 9.4 GW and the company had net cash. The board recommended a ₹1 dividend. The shares rose more than 8% intraday to a 52-week high, then fell about 7.6% on 30 April.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the year confirmed that the IPO-era growth was real, but the sharp swing afterwards showed how volatile the stock is.

events.title: Lock-in on the remaining IPO anchor shares ends, 90 days after allotment
events.details: The lock-in on the second half of the shares allotted to anchor investors in the IPO ended on 12 February 2026, 90 days after allotment; the first half had been freed on 14 December 2025. That allowed those institutions to sell. Promoters, who own about 80% of the company, remain under longer lock-ins tied to their minimum contribution, so the free float stays small.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the end of anchor lock-ins removed one known source of selling pressure; low free float still makes the stock prone to sharp moves.

events.title: Q3 FY26: revenue up 118% to ₹1,152 Cr, PAT up 166% to ₹264 Cr; module capacity reaches 10.3 GW
events.details: For the December 2025 quarter, revenue from operations rose 118% year on year to ₹1,152.3 crore, EBITDA rose 105% to ₹413.4 crore, a 35.9% margin, and profit after tax rose 166% to ₹263.6 crore. Nine-month profit was ₹689.2 crore, up 326%. A 2.5 GW module line at Sulibele was commissioned on 20 December 2025, taking module capacity to 10.3 GW. The order book stood at 9.3 GW.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the first quarterly results after listing confirmed the growth story and supported the stock's January rally.

events.title: Jefferies starts coverage with Buy and ₹320 target; stock hits 10% upper circuit, up 17% in two days
events.details: Jefferies initiated coverage of Emmvee with a Buy rating and a ₹320 target, calling it too cheap to ignore and noting that it traded at roughly a 50% discount to listed peers. It valued the company at nine times forward EV/EBITDA. The shares hit the 10% upper circuit and rose about 17% over two sessions. It was the first major foreign broker initiation since the November 2025 listing.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the initiation turned a muted IPO into a rally, and Jefferies has remained the most influential voice on the stock.

events.title: Subsidiary wins 4.5 GWp TOPCon cell supply deal to 2030; pays ₹212 Cr for 6 GW plant land
events.details: Emmvee Energy, the main manufacturing subsidiary, signed an agreement to supply 4.5 GWp of TOPCon solar cells to an unnamed domestic buyer, with deliveries from December 2025 to 2030. The company said the contract was at arm's length with no promoter-group involvement. It also paid about ₹211.58 crore to the Karnataka industrial development board for land for a 6 GW integrated cell and module plant near Bengaluru. First-half FY26 revenue was ₹2,159 crore and profit ₹425.5 crore.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a multi-year cell contract gives visibility for the cell lines, which carry the highest margins.

events.title: Lists flat at ₹217 after a ₹2,900 Cr IPO that was subscribed just 1.02 times
events.details: Emmvee's shares began trading on 18 November 2025 at ₹217, the top of the ₹206–217 price band, on both NSE and BSE. The ₹2,900 crore issue was subscribed only 1.02 times overall: 1.33 times by institutions, 1.16 times by retail investors and 0.32 times by high-net-worth investors. The grey-market premium had fallen to zero by listing day. Part of the proceeds went to repaying debt of the company and its subsidiary Emmvee Energy.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the weak debut set a low base that later results and broker coverage built on.
